lines.text: Hidden dragon. Do not act.
lines.xiang: The yang is below.

lines.text: Dragon appearing in the field. It furthers one to see the great person.
lines.xiang: Virtue extends widely.

lines.text: All day long the superior person is creatively active. In the evening he is still like a corpse. No blame.
lines.xiang: Following the way back and forth.

lines.text: Wavering flight over the depths. No blame.
lines.xiang: Advancing without blame.

lines.text: Flying dragon in the heavens. It furthers one to see the great person.
lines.xiang: The great person creates.

lines.text: Arrogant dragon will have cause to repent.
lines.xiang: Fullness cannot last long.

lines.text: When there is hoarfrost underfoot, solid ice is not far off.
lines.xiang: By gentleness the way is followed, leading to solid ice.

lines.text: Straight, square, great. Without purpose, yet nothing remains unfurthered.
lines.xiang: The way of the earth is bright.

lines.text: Hidden lines. One is able to remain persevering. If by chance you are in the service of a king, seek not works, but bring to completion.
lines.xiang: Knowledge is broad and bright.

lines.text: A tied sack. No blame, no praise.
lines.xiang: Caution brings no harm.

lines.text: A yellow lower garment brings supreme good fortune.
lines.xiang: Culture is within.

lines.text: Dragons fight in the meadow. Their blood is black and yellow.
lines.xiang: The way is exhausted.

lines.text: Hesitation and hindrance. It furthers one to abide in perseverance and to appoint helpers.
lines.xiang: Although there is hesitation and hindrance, the will is correct.

lines.text: Difficulties pile up. Horse and wagon part. He is not a robber; he wants to woo when the time comes. The young girl is chaste, she does not pledge herself. Ten years, then she pledges herself.
lines.xiang: The difficulty of the six in the second place comes from riding on the firm.

lines.text: Whoever hunts deer without the forester only loses his way in the forest. The superior person understands the signs of the time and prefers to desist. To go on brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: One prefers to desist, not pursuing the fleeing game.

lines.text: Horse and wagon part; they seek union. Going brings good fortune. Nothing that would not further.
lines.xiang: Seeking and going brings light.

lines.text: Difficulties in blessing. A little perseverance brings good fortune. Great perseverance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Blessing has not yet been bestowed.

lines.text: Horse and wagon part; weeping tears of blood.
lines.xiang: How can this last long?

lines.text: To make a fool develop it furthers one to apply discipline. The fetters should be removed. To go on in this way brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: It furthers one to apply discipline, thereby correcting the law.

lines.text: To bear with fools in kindliness brings good fortune. To know how to take care of women brings good fortune. The young person is manageable.
lines.xiang: The young person is manageable; firm and yielding unite.

lines.text: Do not seek a person in the marriage market. If one sees a person of bronze, one loses the person of gold. Nothing that would further.
lines.xiang: Do not seek a person in the marriage market, for the conduct is not correct.

lines.text: Entangled folly brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: The humiliation of entangled folly comes from being far from reality.

lines.text: Childlike folly brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of childlike folly comes from yielding gentleness.

lines.text: In punishing folly it does not further one to commit transgressions. The only thing that furthers is to prevent transgressions.
lines.xiang: To prevent transgressions brings good fortune; above and below are in harmony.

lines.text: Waiting in the meadow. It furthers one to abide in what endures. No blame.
lines.xiang: Waiting in the meadow means not running into danger.

lines.text: Waiting on the sand. There is some gossip. The end brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Waiting on the sand means remaining in the center.

lines.text: Waiting in the mud brings about the arrival of enemies.
lines.xiang: The arrival of enemies comes from inviting them by one's own fault. If one is cautious, no defeat follows.

lines.text: Waiting in blood. Get out of the cave.
lines.xiang: One follows yielding obedience.

lines.text: Waiting at meat and drink. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Meat and drink bring good fortune because of the central and correct position.

lines.text: One falls into the cave. Three uninvited guests arrive. Honor them, and in the end there will be good fortune.
lines.xiang: Although the place is not correct, there is no great mistake.

lines.text: If one does not perpetuate the affair, there is a little gossip. In the end, good fortune comes.
lines.xiang: Not perpetuating the affair means that a dispute cannot be drawn out.

lines.text: One cannot engage in conflict; one comes back, gives way, and retreats. With the people of his town, three hundred households, one avoids calamity.
lines.xiang: Not engaging in conflict but returning to give way, one hides in the town.

lines.text: To nourish oneself on ancient virtue induces perseverance. Danger. In the end, good fortune comes. If by chance you are in the service of a king, seek not works.
lines.xiang: Nourishing oneself on ancient virtue means following that which is above brings good fortune.

lines.text: One cannot engage in conflict. One turns back, submits to fate, changes one's attitude, and finds peace in perseverance. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Turning back, submitting to fate, changing one's attitude, and finding peace in perseverance means not losing anything.

lines.text: To contend before him brings supreme good fortune.
lines.xiang: To contend before him brings supreme good fortune because of the central and correct position.

lines.text: Even if by chance a leather belt is bestowed on one, by the end of the morning it will be taken away three times.
lines.xiang: Receiving the belt through contention is not worthy of respect.

lines.text: An army must set forth in the proper order. If the order is not good, misfortune threatens.
lines.xiang: An army setting forth in proper order means that one loses the order to bring misfortune.

lines.text: In the midst of the army. Good fortune. No blame. The king bestows a triple decoration.
lines.xiang: In the midst of the army brings good fortune because of receiving favor from heaven.

lines.text: Perchance the army carries corpses in the wagon. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The army carrying corpses in the wagon means great lack of success.

lines.text: The army retreats. No blame.
lines.xiang: The army retreats without blame because it has not deviated from the normal.

lines.text: There is game in the field. It furthers one to catch it. Without blame. Let the eldest lead the army. The younger transports corpses; then perseverance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Letting the eldest lead the army means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: The great prince issues commands, founds states, vests families with fiefs. Inferior people should not be employed.
lines.xiang: The great prince issues commands in order to rectify achievements.

lines.text: Hold to him in truth and loyalty; no blame. Truth, like a full earthen bowl: thus in the end good fortune comes from without.
lines.xiang: In the beginning of Holding Together, the other brings good fortune.

lines.text: Hold to him inwardly. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Holding to him inwardly means not losing oneself.

lines.text: You hold together with the wrong people.
lines.xiang: Holding together with the wrong people is indeed hurtful.

lines.text: Hold to him outwardly also. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Holding outwardly to the worthy means following the superior.

lines.text: Manifestation of holding together. In the hunt the king uses beaters on three sides only and forgoes game that runs off in front. The people need no warning. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the manifestation of holding together comes from the central and correct position.

lines.text: He finds no head for holding together. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: He finds no head for holding together; there is no end.

9.name: The Taming Power of the Small

lines.text: Return to the way. How could there be blame in this? Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Returning to the way, the meaning is good fortune.

lines.text: He allows himself to be drawn into returning. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Being drawn into returning in the center means not losing oneself.

lines.text: The spokes burst out of the wagon. Man and wife roll their eyes.
lines.xiang: Man and wife roll their eyes because they cannot set their house in order.

lines.text: If you are sincere, blood vanishes and fear gives way. No blame.
lines.xiang: If you are sincere, fear gives way because of agreement in will above.

lines.text: If you are sincere and loyally attached, you are rich in your neighbor.
lines.xiang: If you are sincere and loyally attached, you are not alone in your riches.

lines.text: The rain comes, there is rest. This is due to the lasting effect of character. Perseverance of the woman brings danger. The moon is nearly full. If the superior person continues on, misfortune comes.
lines.xiang: The rain comes and there is rest, thus virtue is accumulated.

lines.text: Simple conduct. Progress without blame.
lines.xiang: Progress of simple conduct means acting according to one's own will alone.

lines.text: Treading a smooth, level course. The perseverance of a dark person brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The perseverance of a dark person brings good fortune because he does not confuse himself.

lines.text: A one-eyed person is able to see; a lame person is able to tread. Treading on the tail of the tiger, it bites. Misfortune. A brave soldier acts the part of a great lord.
lines.xiang: A one-eyed person is able to see, but not enough to see clearly.

lines.text: Treading on the tail of the tiger. Cautious and apprehensive, in the end one will be lucky.
lines.xiang: Cautious and apprehensive, in the end one will be lucky, for the will is carried out.

lines.text: Resolute conduct. Perseverance with awareness of danger.
lines.xiang: Resolute conduct with awareness of danger means the place is correct.

lines.text: Look to your conduct and weigh the favorable signs. When it is full and good, then turning back brings supreme good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Supreme good fortune above brings great celebration.

lines.text: When ribbon grass is pulled up, the sod comes with it. Each according to his kind. Undertakings bring good fortune.
lines.xiang: Undertakings bring good fortune because the will is directed outward.

lines.text: Bearing with the uncultivated, fording the river without a boat, not forgetting the deserted, not losing the nomads. It furthers one to take action in the center.
lines.xiang: Bearing with the uncultivated and taking action in the center means brightening and extending.

lines.text: No plain not followed by a slope. No going not followed by a return. He who remains persevering in danger is without blame. Do not complain about this truth; enjoy the good fortune you still possess.
lines.xiang: No going not followed by a return means the boundary of heaven and earth.

lines.text: Fluttering, fluttering, yet never falling down. Because of the neighbors, one is lavish with one's possessions.
lines.xiang: Fluttering, fluttering, yet never falling down means all lose reality.

lines.text: Emperor Yi gave his daughter in marriage. Supreme good fortune comes.
lines.xiang: Supreme good fortune comes because the central action is carried out according to the will.

lines.text: The wall falls back into the moat. Use no army now. Make your commands known within your own town. Perseverance brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: The wall falling back into the moat means that the order is confused.

lines.text: When ribbon grass is pulled up, the sod comes with it. Perseverance brings good fortune and success.
lines.xiang: Perseverance with ribbon grass brings good fortune because the will is on the ruler.

lines.text: They bear and endure; this means good fortune for inferior people. The standstill serves to help the great person to advance.
lines.xiang: The standstill serves to help the great person to advance because he does not confuse the multitude.

lines.text: They bear shame.
lines.xiang: Bearing shame means the place is not correct.

lines.text: There is command. No blame. Those who work with him are of like kind.
lines.xiang: There is command and no blame because the will is carried out.

lines.text: Standstill is giving way. Good fortune for the great person. What if it should fail, what if it should fail? In this way he ties it to a cluster of mulberry shoots.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the great person comes from the correct place.

lines.text: The standstill comes to an end. First standstill, then good fortune.
lines.xiang: Standstill coming to an end means how could it last long?

lines.text: Fellowship with men at the gate. No blame.
lines.xiang: Going out of the gate for fellowship with men, who could blame him?

lines.text: Fellowship with men in the clan. Humiliation.
lines.xiang: Fellowship with men in the clan is the way of humiliation.

lines.text: He hides weapons in the thicket; he climbs the high hill in front. For three years he does not rise up.
lines.xiang: Hiding weapons in the thicket means the enemy is firm.

lines.text: He climbs up on his wall; he cannot attack. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Climbing up on the wall, he finds it right not to attack.

lines.text: Men bound in fellowship first weep and lament, but afterward they laugh. After great struggles they succeed in meeting.
lines.xiang: Fellowship of men first weeping and lamenting means the firm is in the middle.

lines.text: Fellowship with men in the meadow. No regret.
lines.xiang: Fellowship with men in the meadow means the will has not yet been attained.

lines.text: No relationship with harmful things. Strong in one's integrity. No blame.
lines.xiang: No relationship with harmful things in the beginning of Possession in Great Measure means no harmful contact.

lines.text: A big wagon for loading. One may undertake something. No blame.
lines.xiang: A big wagon for loading means accumulating in the center without defeat.

lines.text: A prince offers it to the Son of Heaven. A petty person cannot do this.
lines.xiang: A prince offering it to the Son of Heaven means the petty person brings harm.

lines.text: He makes a difference between himself and his neighbor. No blame.
lines.xiang: Making a difference between himself and his neighbor brings no blame because of clear discrimination.

lines.text: His sincerity gives him the power to inspire confidence. Kindness without blame.
lines.xiang: His sincerity inspiring confidence means trust extends the will.

lines.text: He is blessed by heaven. Good fortune. Nothing that does not further.
lines.xiang: Supreme good fortune above comes from the protection of heaven.

lines.text: A modest person who sets out to cross the great water brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: A modest person brings good fortune because he is humble and cultivates himself.

lines.text: Modesty that comes to expression. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Modesty that comes to expression and brings good fortune means the heart finds the center.

lines.text: A modest person who accomplishes works of merit brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: A modest person who accomplishes works of merit brings good fortune because the myriad people submit.

lines.text: Nothing that would not further modesty in movement.
lines.xiang: Nothing that would not further modesty in movement means not violating the law.

lines.text: Not increasing whatever one has. With one's neighbors it is beneficial to go to war. Nothing that would not further.
lines.xiang: It is beneficial to go to war in order to punish those who do not submit.

lines.text: Modesty that comes to expression. It is favorable to set armies marching to chastise one's own city and one's own country.
lines.xiang: Modesty that comes to expression means the will has not yet been attained.

lines.text: Enthusiasm that expresses itself brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Enthusiasm that expresses itself brings misfortune because the will is exhausted.

lines.text: Firm as a rock. Not a whole day. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Not a whole day; perseverance brings good fortune because of the central and correct position.

lines.text: Enthusiasm that looks upward brings repentance. Hesitation brings repentance.
lines.xiang: Enthusiasm that looks upward brings repentance because the place is not correct.

lines.text: The source of enthusiasm. He achieves great things. Do not doubt. Friends gather around him as in a hair clasp.
lines.xiang: The source of enthusiasm bringing great achievements means the will is carried out greatly.

lines.text: With constant perseverance there is illness, but it does not die.
lines.xiang: Illness through constant perseverance means yielding rides on the firm.

lines.text: Enthusiasm that has become dark. Perseverance brings uneasiness, but there is no blame.
lines.xiang: Enthusiasm that has become dark above means how can it last long?

lines.text: The standard is changing. Perseverance brings good fortune. To go out of the door in company produces deeds.
lines.xiang: The standard changing means following what brings good fortune.

lines.text: If one clings to the little boy, one loses the strong man.
lines.xiang: If one clings to the little boy, one cannot have both.

lines.text: If one clings to the strong man, one loses the little boy. Following leads to finding what one seeks, but it furthers one to remain persevering.
lines.xiang: If one clings to the strong man, the will is set on the lower.

lines.text: Following leads to obtaining. But should it continue? If one follows the way, there is no blame.
lines.xiang: Following leads to obtaining, but the meaning is ominous.

lines.text: Sincere in the good. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Sincere in the good brings good fortune because of the central and correct position.

lines.text: The king offers his sacrifice on the Western Mountain. Good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: He is tied and bound in following, and it is proper to offer sacrifice.

18.name: Work on What Has Been Spoiled

lines.text: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father. If there is a son, no blame rests on the departed father. Danger. In the end, good fortune.
lines.xiang: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father means the will is directed toward the father.

lines.text: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's mother. One must not be too persevering.
lines.xiang: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's mother means finding the middle way.

lines.text: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father. There is a little regret but no great blame.
lines.xiang: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father means finally there is no blame.

lines.text: Tolerating what has been spoiled by one's father. In continuing one sees humiliation.
lines.xiang: Tolerating what has been spoiled by one's father means going forth and not obtaining.

lines.text: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father. One meets with praise.
lines.xiang: Setting right what has been spoiled by one's father means receiving praise through virtue.

lines.text: He serves not king and state; he excels in exalting his own calling.
lines.xiang: Not serving king and state means the will can be a model.

lines.text: Joint approach. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Joint approach with perseverance brings good fortune because the will is correct.

lines.text: Joint approach. Good fortune. Everything furthers.
lines.xiang: Joint approach bringing good fortune and everything furthering means not yet obeying the command.

lines.text: Comfortable approach. Nothing that would further. If one is stimulated, there is no blame.
lines.xiang: Comfortable approach means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Complete approach. No blame.
lines.xiang: Complete approach without blame means the place is correct.

lines.text: Wise approach. This is great for a prince. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: What is great for a prince means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: Greathearted approach. Good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Greathearted approach brings good fortune because the will is within.

lines.text: Boylike contemplation. For an inferior person, no blame. For a superior person, humiliation.
lines.xiang: Boylike contemplation of the inferior person means the way of the inferior person.

lines.text: Contemplation through the crack of the door. Furthering for the perseverance of a woman.
lines.xiang: Contemplation through the crack of the door for the perseverance of a woman means it is also a disgrace.

lines.text: Contemplation of my life decides the choice between advance and retreat.
lines.xiang: Contemplation of my life deciding advance and retreat means not losing the way.

lines.text: Contemplation of the light of the kingdom. It furthers one to exert influence as a guest of the king.
lines.xiang: Contemplation of the light of the kingdom means esteeming the guest.

lines.text: Contemplation of my life. The superior person is without blame.
lines.xiang: Contemplation of my life means observing the people.

lines.text: Contemplation of his life. The superior person is without blame.
lines.xiang: Contemplation of his life means the will is not yet peaceful.

lines.text: His feet are fastened in the stocks, and his toes disappear. No blame.
lines.xiang: Feet fastened in the stocks mean he cannot walk.

lines.text: Bites on dried meat and burns his nose. No blame.
lines.xiang: Biting on dried meat and burning his nose means riding on the firm.

lines.text: Bites on old dried meat and strikes on something poisonous. Slight humiliation. No blame.
lines.xiang: Striking on something poisonous means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Bites on dried gristly meat. Receives metal arrows. It furthers one to be aware of difficulties. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: It furthers one to be aware of difficulties because the light is not yet shining.

lines.text: Bites on dried lean meat. Receives yellow gold. Perseverance brings danger. No blame.
lines.xiang: Perseverance bringing no blame means obtaining what is appropriate.

lines.text: His neck is fastened in the wooden cangue, and his ears disappear. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The neck fastened in the wooden cangue means the ears are not clear.

lines.text: He lends grace to his toes, leaves the carriage, and walks.
lines.xiang: Leaving the carriage to walk means righteously he does not ride.

lines.text: He lends grace to his beard.
lines.xiang: He lends grace to his beard because he rises with what is above.

lines.text: Graceful and moist. Constant perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of constant perseverance means there is no one to humiliate him.

lines.text: Grace or simplicity? A white horse comes as if on wings. He is not a robber; he will woo at the right time.
lines.xiang: The six in the fourth place is in doubt.

lines.text: Grace in gardens and hillocks. The roll of silk is meager and small. Humiliation, but in the end good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the fifth place brings joy.

lines.text: Simple grace. No blame.
lines.xiang: Simple grace without blame means above one attains his will.

lines.text: The leg of the couch is split. Those who persevere are destroyed. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The leg of the couch split means destroying that which is below.

lines.text: The couch is split to the frame. Those who persevere are destroyed. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The couch split to the frame means there is no correspondence.

lines.text: He splits with them. No blame.
lines.xiang: He splits with them without blame because he loses those above and below.

lines.text: The couch is split to the skin. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The couch split to the skin means the misfortune is near at hand.

lines.text: A string of fish. The palace ladies rule. There is advantage in all things.
lines.xiang: The palace ladies ruling means finally there is no fault.

lines.text: The great fruit is not eaten. The superior person receives a carriage. The inferior person is destroyed beneath the palace.
lines.xiang: The superior person receiving a carriage means he is carried by the people.

lines.text: Return from a short distance. No need for remorse. Great good fortune.
lines.xiang: Return from a short distance means cultivating oneself.

lines.text: Quiet return. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of quiet return comes from the yielding below.

lines.text: Repeated return. Danger. No blame.
lines.xiang: Repeated return bringing danger means the meaning is without blame.

lines.text: Walking in the midst of others, one returns alone.
lines.xiang: Walking in the midst of others and returning alone means following the way.

lines.text: Noblehearted return. No remorse.
lines.xiang: Noblehearted return without remorse means self-examination in the center.

lines.text: Lost return. Misfortune. There is calamity and affliction. If one should set armies marching, in the end he will suffer a great defeat; and for the king, misfortune. For ten years he cannot attack again.
lines.xiang: The misfortune of lost return means one turns against the way of the ruler.

lines.text: Innocent action brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Innocent action bringing good fortune means the will is carried out.

lines.text: One who plows not nor sows reaps a harvest, though it be not his own field. It furthers one to have somewhere to go.
lines.xiang: One who plows not nor sows is not yet rich.

lines.text: Undeserved misfortune. A cow is tied to a tree. The traveler's cow is taken; the townsman's calamity.
lines.xiang: The traveler's cow being taken brings calamity to the townsman.

lines.text: He who can be persevering remains without blame.
lines.xiang: Remaining without blame means holding fast to what is one's own.

lines.text: Use no medicine in an illness incurred through no fault of your own. It will pass of itself.
lines.xiang: Use no medicine for an illness incurred through no fault; it cannot be tested.

lines.text: Innocent action brings misfortune. Nothing that would further.
lines.xiang: Innocent action bringing misfortune means disaster from exhaustion.

26.name: The Taming Power of the Great

lines.text: Danger is at hand. It furthers one to desist.
lines.xiang: Danger at hand and desisting means not running into disaster.

lines.text: The axletree is split.
lines.xiang: The axletree split means there is no fault in the center.

lines.text: A good horse that follows others. Awareness of danger, with perseverance, furthers. Practice chariot driving and armed defense daily. It furthers one to have somewhere to go.
lines.xiang: It furthers one to have somewhere to go because the will above is united.

lines.text: The headboard of a young bull. Great good fortune.
lines.xiang: Great good fortune of the six in the fourth place means there is joy.

lines.text: The tusks of a gelded boar. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the fifth place brings celebration.

lines.text: Heavenly gates. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Heavenly gates bringing good fortune means the way is greatly carried out.

lines.text: You let your magic tortoise go, and look at me with the corners of your mouth drooping. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Looking at me with the corners of your mouth drooping means it is not worth esteeming.

lines.text: Turning to the summit for nourishment, deviating from the way to seek nourishment from the hill. Advance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Advance of the six in the second place brings misfortune because the conduct loses its kind.

lines.text: Turning away from nourishment. Perseverance brings misfortune. Ten years will pass before there is any use for it. Nothing that would further.
lines.xiang: Ten years of uselessness means going greatly against the way.

lines.text: Turning to the summit for nourishment brings good fortune. He who keeps looking with a tiger's vigilance without blinking. There is no blame.
lines.xiang: Turning to the summit for nourishment bringing good fortune means what is above bestows brightness.

lines.text: Turning away from the path. Perseverance at home brings good fortune. It should not cross the great water.
lines.xiang: Perseverance at home bringing good fortune means following and yielding to what is above.

lines.text: The source of nourishment. Awareness of danger brings good fortune. It furthers one to cross the great water.
lines.xiang: The source of nourishment bringing good fortune means there is great celebration.

lines.text: Place a mat of white grass beneath. No blame.
lines.xiang: Placing a mat of white grass beneath means yielding is below.

lines.text: A withered poplar puts forth flowers. An older man takes a young wife. Nothing that would not further.
lines.xiang: An older man taking a young wife means passing over and uniting.

lines.text: The ridgepole sags to the breaking point. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The ridgepole sagging to the breaking point means there is nothing to help.

lines.text: The ridgepole is braced. Good fortune. If there are ulterior motives, it is humiliating.
lines.xiang: The ridgepole being braced bringing good fortune means it does not sag below.

lines.text: A withered poplar puts forth leaves. An older woman takes a young husband. No blame, no praise.
lines.xiang: A withered poplar putting forth leaves means how can it last long?

lines.text: One must go through the water. It goes over one's head. Misfortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: The misfortune of going through the water that goes over one's head cannot be blamed on anyone.

lines.text: Repetition of the Abysmal. In the abyss one falls into a pit. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Repetition of the Abysmal and falling into a pit means losing the way brings misfortune.

lines.text: The abyss is dangerous. One achieves small things.
lines.xiang: Achieving small things means not yet emerging from the center.

lines.text: Coming upon the abyss, ahead an abyss, behind a dangerous height. When one enters a cave in a pit, there is misfortune.
lines.xiang: Coming upon the abyss means finally without success.

lines.text: A jug of wine, a basket of food, with these earthen vessels a simple offering. Accepting this through the window. No blame in the end.
lines.xiang: A jug of wine and a basket of food means the firm and yielding meet.

lines.text: The abyss does not overflow. It is filled only to the level of the ridge. No blame.
lines.xiang: The abyss not overflowing means the center is not yet great.

lines.text: Bound with cords and ropes, shut in between thorn-hedged prison walls. For three years one does not find the way. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The six at the top losing the way means misfortune for three years.

lines.text: The footsteps are tangled. One creates disorder but there is no blame.
lines.xiang: Tangled footsteps mean one shuns blame.

lines.text: Yellow light. Supreme good fortune.
lines.xiang: Yellow light bringing supreme good fortune means finding the middle way.

lines.text: In the light of the setting sun, men beat their pots and sing. The big men lament. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The light of the setting sun means how can it last long?

lines.text: Its coming is sudden; it flames up, dies down, is thrown away.
lines.xiang: Its coming is sudden means there is no place for it.

lines.text: Tears in floods, sighing and lamenting. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the fifth place means cleaving to the ruler.

lines.text: The king uses him to march forth and chastise. Then it is best to cut off the heads and not to keep the prisoners. No blame.
lines.xiang: The king using him to march forth means to correct the country.

lines.text: Influence on the big toe.
lines.xiang: Influence on the big toe means the will is directed outward.

lines.text: Influence on the calves of the legs. Misfortune. Abiding brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Although there is misfortune, abiding brings good fortune because yielding does no harm.

lines.text: Influence on the thighs. Holding to that which follows blindly brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: Influence on the thighs means not resting in the place.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. The fluttering thoughts come and go. Friends follow your thoughts.
lines.xiang: Perseverance bringing good fortune and remorse disappearing means unharmed by stimulation.

lines.text: Influence on the back of the neck. No remorse.
lines.xiang: Influence on the back of the neck means the will is directed to the end.

lines.text: Influence on the jaws, cheeks, and tongue.
lines.xiang: Influence on the jaws, cheeks, and tongue means speaking from the mouth.

lines.text: Seeking duration too hastily brings misfortune. Nothing that would further.
lines.xiang: Seeking duration too hastily brings misfortune because one seeks it too deeply from the start.

lines.text: Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Remorse disappearing of the nine in the second place means being able to last in the center.

lines.text: He who does not give duration to his character meets with disgrace. Persistent humiliation.
lines.xiang: He who does not give duration to his character meets with disgrace because there is nowhere to go.

lines.text: No game in the field.
lines.xiang: No game in the field means one is not in the right place long.

lines.text: Giving duration to one's character. Perseverance brings good fortune for a woman. Misfortune for a man.
lines.xiang: Good fortune for a woman means following to the end.

lines.text: Restlessness brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Restlessness at the top brings no success.

lines.text: Retreat at the tail. Danger. It does not further one to undertake anything.
lines.xiang: The danger of retreat at the tail means not going; what disaster could there be?

lines.text: He holds him fast with yellow oxhide. No one can tear him loose.
lines.xiang: He holds him fast with yellow oxhide means the will is firm.

lines.text: A halted retreat is nerve-wracking and dangerous. To retain people as men- and maidservants brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The nerve-wracking danger of a halted retreat means there is sickness and exhaustion.

lines.text: Voluntary retreat brings good fortune to the superior person and downfall to the inferior person.
lines.xiang: The superior person's voluntary retreat means the inferior person cannot do it.

lines.text: Friendly retreat. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Friendly retreat bringing good fortune means the will is correct.

lines.text: Cheerful retreat. Everything serves to further.
lines.xiang: Cheerful retreat serving to further everything means there is no doubt.

lines.text: Power in the toes. Continuing brings misfortune. This is certainly true.
lines.xiang: Power in the toes means the certainty is exhausted.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Perseverance of the nine in the second place brings good fortune because it is in the middle.

lines.text: The inferior person uses power. The superior person uses influence. Perseverance brings danger. A ram butts against the fence and entangles his horns.
lines.xiang: The inferior person uses power; the superior person refrains.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. The fence opens up. He does not entangle his horns. The power is in the axle of a big wagon.
lines.xiang: The fence opening up means going forward is supported.

lines.text: Loses the goat in the field. No remorse.
lines.xiang: Losing the goat in the field means the place is not correct.

lines.text: A ram butts against the fence. He cannot retreat, he cannot go forward. Nothing serves to further. If one notes the difficulty, this brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Not being able to retreat or go forward means there is no auspicious sign.

lines.text: Progress that meets with confidence brings good fortune. If one is fearful and anxious, it brings good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Progress meeting with confidence means acting alone is correct.

lines.text: Progress that meets with sorrow. Perseverance brings good fortune. One receives this great blessing from one's grandmother.
lines.xiang: Receiving this great blessing means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: All are in agreement. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: All being in agreement means the will moves upward.

lines.text: Progress like a hamster. Perseverance brings danger.
lines.xiang: Progress like a hamster means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Remorse disappears. Do not trouble about gain or loss. Going forward brings good fortune. Everything serves to further.
lines.xiang: Not troubling about gain or loss means going forward brings blessing.

lines.text: Progress with one's horns. It is permissible to use force only to chastise one's own city. Danger. Good fortune. No blame. But perseverance brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: It is permissible to use force only to chastise one's own city because the way is not yet bright.

lines.text: Darkening of the light during flight. He drops his wings. The superior person walks for three days without eating. He has a place to go. The host has things to say.
lines.xiang: The superior person walking and not eating means it is right not to eat.

lines.text: Darkening of the light injures the left thigh. He saves himself with the strength of a horse. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the second place means acting in accordance with the law.

lines.text: Darkening of the light during the hunt in the south. Their great leader is captured. One should not act hastily to make things right.
lines.xiang: The will of the hunt in the south means great attainment.

lines.text: He penetrates the left side of the belly. One gets at the very heart of darkening of the light and leaves the gate and courtyard.
lines.xiang: Penetrating the left side of the belly means getting at the heart of the matter.

lines.text: Darkening of the light as with Chi. Perseverance furthers.
lines.xiang: The perseverance of Chi means brightness cannot be extinguished.

lines.text: Not light but dark. First he climbed up to heaven, then he plunged into the depths of the earth.
lines.xiang: First climbing up to heaven means illuminating the four countries.

lines.text: Firm seclusion within the family. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Firm seclusion within the family means the will has not yet changed.

lines.text: She should not follow her whims. She must attend within to the food. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the second place means yielding to what is above.

lines.text: When tempers flare up in the family, too much severity brings remorse. Good fortune comes from the woman and child laughing and chatting.
lines.xiang: When the family is stern, one is not lost.

lines.text: She is the treasure of the house. Great good fortune.
lines.xiang: She is the treasure of the house, and all is favorable.

lines.text: As a king he approaches his family. Fear not. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: As a king he approaches his family, and they love each other.

lines.text: His work commands respect. In the end good fortune comes.
lines.xiang: His work commanding respect means turning back upon oneself.

lines.text: Remorse disappears. If you lose your horse, do not run after it; it will return of itself. When you see an evil person, guard yourself against mistakes.
lines.xiang: Seeing an evil person means guarding oneself to avoid blame.

lines.text: One meets his lord in a narrow street. No blame.
lines.xiang: Meeting one's lord in a narrow street means not having lost the way.

lines.text: One sees the wagon dragged back, the oxen hindered, the man's hair and nose cut off. Not a good beginning, but a good end.
lines.xiang: Seeing the wagon dragged back means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Isolated through opposition, one meets a person of like kind. Though he is a relative, there is danger. No blame.
lines.xiang: Meeting a person of like kind brings no blame because the will is carried out.

lines.text: Remorse disappears. The companion bites his way through the wrappings. If one goes to him, how could it be a mistake?
lines.xiang: Biting through the wrappings means going forward brings celebration.

lines.text: Isolated through opposition, one sees his companion as a pig covered with dirt, as a wagon full of devils. First he draws his bow against him, then he lays it aside. He is not a robber; he will woo at the right time. Going forward, encountering rain, brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Encountering rain brings good fortune because all doubts are dispelled.

lines.text: Going leads to obstruction, coming brings praise.
lines.xiang: Going leads to obstruction, coming brings praise; it is right to wait.

lines.text: The king's minister suffers obstruction upon obstruction, but it is not his own fault.
lines.xiang: The king's minister suffering obstruction upon obstruction means finally there is no fault.

lines.text: Going leads to obstruction; he comes back.
lines.xiang: Going leads to obstruction and he comes back; those within rejoice.

lines.text: Going leads to obstruction; he comes back and submits to his superior.
lines.xiang: Going leads to obstruction and he comes back to submit; this is the position of reality.

lines.text: In the midst of the greatest obstruction, friends come.
lines.xiang: In the midst of the greatest obstruction, friends come because of the central position.

lines.text: Going leads to obstruction; he comes back in a great flow. Good fortune. It furthers one to see the great person.
lines.xiang: Going leads to obstruction and he comes back in a great flow; the will is within.

lines.text: Without blame.
lines.xiang: At the meeting of firm and yielding, there is no blame.

lines.text: One kills three foxes in the field and receives a yellow arrow. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Perseverance of the nine in the second place brings good fortune because he obtains the middle way.

lines.text: If a man carries a burden on his back and nonetheless rides in a carriage, he thereby encourages robbers to draw near. Perseverance brings humiliation.
lines.xiang: Riding in a carriage when carrying a burden means it is also a disgrace.

lines.text: Deliver yourself from your great toe. Then the companion comes, and one is trusted.
lines.xiang: Delivering from the great toe means the place is not correct.

lines.text: If only the superior person can deliver himself, it brings good fortune. He thus proves his confidence in inferior people.
lines.xiang: If the superior person delivers himself, the inferior person withdraws.

lines.text: A prince shoots at a hawk on a high wall. He kills it. Everything serves to further.
lines.xiang: A prince shooting at a hawk means delivering from rebellion.

lines.text: Going quickly when one's work is finished brings no blame. One must consider how much one may decrease others.
lines.xiang: Going quickly when one's work is finished means holding fast to the will.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Going brings misfortune. Without decreasing oneself, one is able to increase others.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of perseverance of the nine in the second place comes from acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: When three people journey together, their number decreases by one. When one person journeys alone, he finds a companion.
lines.xiang: One person journeying alone finding a companion means that when three are doubtful, one is doubtful.

lines.text: If a man decreases his faults, he may make others hurry to come with him. No blame.
lines.xiang: Decreasing one's faults is also a cause for joy.

lines.text: Someone does indeed increase him. Ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose it. Supreme good fortune.
lines.xiang: The supreme good fortune of the six in the fifth place comes from blessing from above.

lines.text: If one is increased without diminishing others, there is no blame. Perseverance brings good fortune. It furthers one to undertake something. One obtains servants but no longer has a home.
lines.xiang: If one is increased without diminishing others, it means the great will is carried out.

lines.text: It furthers one to accomplish great deeds. Supreme good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Supreme good fortune and no blame means the inferior person does not increase to excess.

lines.text: Someone does indeed increase him. Ten pairs of tortoises cannot oppose it. Constant perseverance brings good fortune. The king presents him before God. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Someone increasing him means it comes from without.

lines.text: One is increased through unfortunate events. No blame, if you are sincere and walk in the middle, and report with a seal to the prince.
lines.xiang: Being increased through unfortunate events means it is by nature so.

lines.text: If you walk in the middle and report to the prince, he will follow. It furthers one to be used in the removal of the capital.
lines.xiang: If he follows, it means the will is increased.

lines.text: If you are sincere and benevolent, there is no need for questions. Supreme good fortune. Sincerity and benevolence are the natural possessions of his own nature.
lines.xiang: Sincerity and benevolence need no questions because the benevolence is in the center.

lines.text: He is increased without being given a gift. He is attacked without being injured. Perseverance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: He is increased without being given a gift; the statement is one-sided.

lines.text: Vigorous in the toes. Going forward brings misfortune if one is not prepared.
lines.xiang: Going forward and not being prepared means there is blame.

lines.text: Alarm cries at night. Armed, no fear.
lines.xiang: There is alarm at night, but no fear means obtaining the middle way.

lines.text: Vigorous in the cheekbones brings misfortune. The superior person is fully resolved. He walks alone and encounters the rain, to his disadvantage, but there is no blame.
lines.xiang: The superior person is fully resolved; finally there is no blame.

lines.text: There is no skin on his thighs, and walking is difficult. If he were to lead sheep, they would not follow. If he were to follow, he would not hear words. But if he can be persevering, there will be no blame.
lines.xiang: Walking with difficulty means the place is not correct.

lines.text: In dealing with weeds, firm resolution is necessary. Walking in the middle remains free of blame.
lines.xiang: Walking in the middle without blame means the middle is not yet bright.

lines.text: No cry. In the end there is misfortune.
lines.xiang: The misfortune of no cry means it cannot last long.

lines.text: It must be checked with a brake of bronze. Perseverance brings good fortune. If one lets it go, one sees a pig covered with dirt. There is inconstancy.
lines.xiang: It must be checked with a brake of bronze because the way of the yielding is led along.

lines.text: There is a fish in the bag. No blame. It does not further the guest.
lines.xiang: There is a fish in the bag; the meaning does not extend to the guest.

lines.text: There is no skin on his thighs, and walking is difficult. Danger, but no great blame.
lines.xiang: Walking with difficulty means the act is not led along.

lines.text: No fish in the bag. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The misfortune of no fish in the bag means keeping away from the people.

lines.text: A melon covered with willow leaves. Hidden in it, the thing he needs. It drops down to him from heaven.
lines.xiang: The nine in the fifth place hiding the thing means central correctness.

lines.text: He comes to meet with his horns. Humiliation. No blame.
lines.xiang: He comes to meet with his horns; above, the place is exhausted and humiliating.

lines.text: If you are sincere, but not to the end, there will sometimes be confusion, sometimes gathering together. If you call out, then after one shout of anguish you will laugh. Do not worry. It is without blame.
lines.xiang: Sometimes confusion and sometimes gathering together means the will is confused.

lines.text: If you are sincere, it brings good fortune. No blame. It furthers one to use a small offering in worship.
lines.xiang: If you are sincere and it brings good fortune, it means the center is not changed.

lines.text: If one gathers together with sighs, nothing that would further. Going is without blame. Small humiliation.
lines.xiang: Going is without blame because above is gentle.

lines.text: Great good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Great good fortune without blame means the place is not correct.

lines.text: If in gathering together there is position, no blame. If the unbelieving ones come, there is supreme perseverance. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: If in gathering together there is position, it means the will is not yet shining.

lines.text: Sighing and weeping. No blame.
lines.xiang: Sighing and weeping means not yet at ease above.

lines.text: Pushing upward that meets with confidence brings great good fortune.
lines.xiang: Pushing upward that meets with confidence brings great good fortune because the will is above.

lines.text: If one is sincere, it furthers one to use a small offering in worship. No blame.
lines.xiang: The sincerity of the nine in the second place brings joy.

lines.text: Pushing upward in an empty city.
lines.xiang: Pushing upward in an empty city means there is no doubt.

lines.text: The king makes him a present of his sacrificial food on Mount Ch'i. Good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: The king makes him a present on Mount Ch'i because he serves him with gentleness.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Pushing upward by steps.
lines.xiang: Perseverance brings good fortune in pushing upward by steps means the great will is carried out.

lines.text: Pushing upward in darkness. It furthers one to be unceasingly persevering.
lines.xiang: Pushing upward in darkness at the top means growing, but not enriching.

lines.text: One sits oppressed under a bare tree and strays into a gloomy valley. For three years one sees nothing.
lines.xiang: Entering the gloomy valley means obscurity without light.

lines.text: One is oppressed while at meat and drink. The man with the scarlet knee bands is just coming. It furthers one to offer sacrifice. To set forth brings misfortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: Being oppressed while at meat and drink means there is celebration in the center.

lines.text: One is oppressed by a stone. He leans on a thorn bush. One enters his house and does not see his wife. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Leaning on a thorn bush means riding on the firm.

lines.text: He comes very slowly, oppressed in a golden carriage. Humiliation, but there is an end.
lines.xiang: Coming very slowly means the will is below.

lines.text: His nose and feet are cut off. Oppression at the hands of the man with the purple knee bands. It furthers one to make offerings and to set forth slowly.
lines.xiang: His nose and feet are cut off means the will is not yet attained.

lines.text: He is oppressed by creeping vines. He moves uncertainly and says, "Movement brings remorse." If one feels remorse, going forward brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Being oppressed by creeping vines means the place is not correct.

lines.text: The well is muddy. No one drinks from it. The old well is the home of vermin. No one draws from it. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The well being muddy and undrinkable means it is below.

lines.text: A well is shot with fish and shrimp. The jug is broken and leaks.
lines.xiang: A well shot with fish and shrimp means there is no correspondence.

lines.text: The well is cleaned, but no one drinks from it. This is my heart's sorrow. It would be advantageous to draw water. When the king is bright, all receive the blessing.
lines.xiang: The well cleaned but undrinkable means the heart is sorrowful.

lines.text: The well is being lined. No blame.
lines.xiang: The well being lined without blame means it is being repaired.

lines.text: In the well there is a clear, cold spring from which one can drink.
lines.xiang: The clear, cold spring that can be drunk from means central correctness.

lines.text: One draws from the well without hindrance. It is dependable. Supreme good fortune.
lines.xiang: Supreme good fortune above means great attainment.

lines.text: He is bound with the skin of a yellow ox.
lines.xiang: He is bound with the skin of a yellow ox; one cannot act thus.

lines.text: When one's own day comes, one may create revolution. Starting brings good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: When one's own day comes, starting brings good fortune because the action is meritorious.

lines.text: Starting brings misfortune. Perseverance brings danger. When talk of revolution has gone the round three times, one may commit himself. There is faith.
lines.xiang: When talk of revolution has gone the round three times, it is believed.

lines.text: Remorse disappears. People change their ways. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Changing ways brings good fortune because the will is believed.

lines.text: The great man changes like a tiger. Even before the inquiry, there is faith.
lines.xiang: The great man changes like a tiger; his stripes are clear and bright.

lines.text: The superior person changes like a leopard. The inferior person changes his face. Starting brings misfortune. To remain persevering brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The superior person changes like a leopard; his stripes are rich and glossy.

lines.text: A cauldron with feet upturned. It furthers the removal of stagnating substance. One takes a concubine for the sake of her son. No blame.
lines.xiang: A cauldron with feet upturned means there is no harm in this.

lines.text: There is food in the cauldron. My enemy is envious, but he cannot harm me. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: There is food in the cauldron; one must be cautious about where one goes.

lines.text: The handle of the cauldron is changed. One is impeded in his way of life. The fat of the pheasant is not eaten. Once rain falls, remorse is spent. In the end, good fortune comes.
lines.xiang: The handle of the cauldron changed means losing the right meaning.

lines.text: The legs of the cauldron are broken. The prince's meal is spilled, and his person is soiled. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: The prince's meal spilled means trust is lost. How can this be?

lines.text: The cauldron has yellow handles, golden carrying rings. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The cauldron having yellow handles means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: The carrying rings of the cauldron are jade. Great good fortune. Everything serves to further.
lines.xiang: The jade carrying rings at the top mean the firm and yielding are in proper relation.

lines.text: Thunder comes in the dread hour of night. Fear brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Fear bringing good fortune means fear brings blessing.

lines.text: Thunder comes with a terrible roar. Then it laughs and talks cheerfully. Misfortune. One loses one's possessions for seven days. Then one finds them again.
lines.xiang: The terrible roar means riding on the firm.

lines.text: Thunder comes and is terrifying. He walks to and fro in the terror, but there is no harm.
lines.xiang: Walking to and fro in the terror means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Thunder sinks into the mud.
lines.xiang: Thunder sinking into the mud means the light is not yet shining.

lines.text: Thunder comes to and fro with a terrible roar. He loses his possessions and cows for a hundred days. Then he finds them again.
lines.xiang: Thunder coming to and fro means acting dangerously.

lines.text: Thunder comes shuddering. He looks around in dismay. Misfortune. The thunder does not hit him himself, but hits his neighbor. No blame. The friend has something to say concerning marriage.
lines.xiang: Looking around in dismay means the center is not attained.

lines.text: Keeping his toes still. No blame. Enduring perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: Keeping his toes still means not losing correctness.

lines.text: Keeping his calves still. He cannot rescue him whom he follows. His heart is not glad.
lines.xiang: Not being able to rescue him whom he follows means he does not retreat to listen.

lines.text: Keeping his hips still. Making his sacrum stiff. Danger enters into the heart.
lines.xiang: Making his sacrum stiff means endangering the heart.

lines.text: Keeping his trunk still. No blame.
lines.xiang: Keeping his trunk still means stopping in the body.

lines.text: Keeping his jaws still. The words are orderly. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Keeping his jaws still means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: Noblehearted keeping still. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Noblehearted keeping still brings good fortune because it ends generously.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the shore. The young son is in danger. There is talk. No blame.
lines.xiang: The danger of the young son means there is no blame in the meaning.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the cliff. Eating and drinking in peace and concord. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Eating and drinking in peace and concord means not eating in vain.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the plateau. The husband goes on an expedition and does not return. The wife is with child and does not give birth. Misfortune. It furthers one to fight off robbers.
lines.xiang: The husband going on an expedition means he leaves his kind to go with the ugly.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the tree. One may get a flat branch. No blame.
lines.xiang: One may get a flat branch because the yielding follows.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the summit. For three years the wife has no child. In the end, nothing can hinder her. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: In the end nothing can hinder her; good fortune comes because she obtains what she desires.

lines.text: The wild goose gradually draws near the cloud heights. Its feathers can be used for the sacred dance. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Its feathers can be used for the sacred dance; good fortune means it cannot be disordered.

lines.text: The marrying maiden as a concubine. A lame person who can walk. Going brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The marrying maiden as a concubine means acting with constancy.

lines.text: A one-eyed person who can see. It furthers the perseverance of a secluded person.
lines.xiang: It furthers the perseverance of a secluded person means the constant has not changed.

lines.text: The marrying maiden as a slave. She marries as a concubine.
lines.xiang: The marrying maiden as a slave means the place is not correct.

lines.text: The marrying maiden draws out the time. The marriage is postponed. A late marriage is timed.
lines.xiang: Postponing the time means the will waits for action.

lines.text: The sovereign I gave his daughter in marriage. The embroidered garments of the princess were not so gorgeous as those of the servingmaid. The moon that is nearly full brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The sovereign I gave his daughter in marriage. The embroidered garments were not so gorgeous means her place is in the center and she is modest.

lines.text: The woman holds the basket, but there are no fruits in it. The man stabs the sheep, but no blood flows. Nothing that would further.
lines.xiang: The six at the top holding an empty basket means she receives nothing.

lines.text: He meets his host. Although they are of the same kind, there is no blame. Going brings praise.
lines.xiang: Although they are of the same kind, there is no blame; going past the day brings disaster.

lines.text: He is surrounded by a screen so thick that at noon he can see the Dipper. Going forward brings mistrust and hate. If he rouses himself through the power of the dark, good fortune comes.
lines.xiang: Rousing himself through the power of the dark brings good fortune because he acts sincerely.

lines.text: He is surrounded by a screen so thick that at noon he can see the foam. He breaks his right arm. No blame.
lines.xiang: He breaks his right arm because he cannot undertake anything great.

lines.text: He is surrounded by a screen so thick that at noon he can see the Dipper. He meets his ruler. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The screen so thick that at noon he can see the Dipper means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Lines are coming. Blessing and fame draw near. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six in the fifth place means there is celebration.

lines.text: His house is in a state of abundance. He screens off his family. He looks out through the door and does not see anyone. For three years he sees no one. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: His house in a state of abundance means he flutters about in the heights.

lines.text: The wanderer comes in a mean, petty spirit. This brings misfortune and contempt.
lines.xiang: The wanderer coming in a mean, petty spirit means the will is exhausted and brings disaster.

lines.text: The wanderer comes to an inn. He has his property with him. He receives faithfulness within.
lines.xiang: He has his property with him and receives faithfulness; finally there is no fault.

lines.text: The wanderer's inn burns down. He loses the steadfastness of his young servant. Danger.
lines.xiang: The wanderer's inn burning down means he also suffers hurt.

lines.text: The wanderer rests in a shelter. He obtains his property and an ax. My heart is not glad.
lines.xiang: Resting in a shelter means not having obtained the place.

lines.text: He shoots a pheasant. It drops with the first arrow. In the end this brings praise and reward.
lines.xiang: In the end bringing praise and reward means reaching above.

lines.text: The bird's nest burns up. The wanderer first laughs and then must needs lament and weep. He loses his ox in the course of his adversity. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Taking the position of the wanderer at the top means to burn up is proper.

lines.text: Advance and retreat. It furthers the perseverance of a military man.
lines.xiang: Advance and retreat means the will is in doubt.

lines.text: The gentle lies hidden in the bed. It brings the use of shamans and physicians. Good fortune. No blame.
lines.xiang: The use of shamans and physicians bringing good fortune means obtaining the center.

lines.text: Repeated gentle. Humiliation.
lines.xiang: Repeated gentle bringing humiliation means the will is exhausted.

lines.text: Remorse disappears. In the field one catches game.
lines.xiang: In the field one catches game because there is merit.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. Nothing that does not further. Before the beginning, three days. After the end, three days. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the nine in the fifth place means the place is correct and central.

lines.text: The gentle lies hidden under the bed. He loses his property and his ax. Perseverance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: The gentle lying hidden under the bed means the top is exhausted.

lines.text: Contented joyousness. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: Contented joyousness bringing good fortune means not being confused in going.

lines.text: Sincere joyousness. Good fortune. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Sincere joyousness bringing good fortune means the will is believed.

lines.text: Coming joyousness. Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Coming joyousness bringing misfortune means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Joyousness that is weighed is not at peace. After ridding himself of mistakes, there is delight.
lines.xiang: The delight of the nine in the fourth place brings joy.

lines.text: Sincerity toward decay. It is believable.
lines.xiang: Sincerity toward decay means the place is correct.

lines.text: Seductive joyousness.
lines.xiang: Seductive joyousness at the top means it is not yet shining.

lines.text: He rescues him with a strong horse. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of the six at the beginning means yielding.

lines.text: He hurries to his support with a hundred galloping horses. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Hurrying to his support with a hundred horses means the wish is obtained.

lines.text: He dissolves his self. No remorse.
lines.xiang: He dissolves his self; the will is outward.

lines.text: He dissolves his bond with his group. Supreme good fortune. Dispersion leads in turn to accumulation. This is something that ordinary people do not think of.
lines.xiang: Dissolving the bond with the group brings supreme good fortune because the light is great.

lines.text: His loud cries are dissipated as sweat dissolves. The king dwells in the capital. There is no blame.
lines.xiang: The king dwelling in the capital without blame means he is in the correct position.

lines.text: He dissolves his blood. Departing, keeping at a distance, going out, is without blame.
lines.xiang: He dissolves his blood; he keeps away from harm.

lines.text: Not going out of the door and the courtyard is without blame.
lines.xiang: Not going out of the door and the courtyard means knowing the way of opening and closing.

lines.text: Not going out of the door and the courtyard brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: Not going out of the door and the courtyard bringing misfortune means losing the opportunity to the extreme.

lines.text: He who knows no limitation will have cause to lament. No blame.
lines.xiang: The lamenting of knowing no limitation means who could blame him?

lines.text: Contented limitation. Success.
lines.xiang: Contented limitation bringing success means receiving from above.

lines.text: Sweet limitation brings good fortune. Going on brings one to distinction.
lines.xiang: Sweet limitation bringing good fortune means the place is central.

lines.text: Galling limitation. Perseverance brings misfortune. Remorse disappears.
lines.xiang: Galling limitation brings misfortune because the way is exhausted.

lines.text: Being prepared brings good fortune. If there are secret designs, it is unsettling.
lines.xiang: Being prepared brings good fortune because the will is not yet changed.

lines.text: A crane calling in the shade. Its young answers it. I have a good goblet. I will share it with you.
lines.xiang: Its young answering it means the center wishes this.

lines.text: He finds an opponent. Sometimes he beats the drum, sometimes he stops. Sometimes he cries, sometimes he sings.
lines.xiang: Sometimes beating the drum and sometimes stopping means the place is not correct.

lines.text: The moon is nearly full. The team horse loses one horse. No blame.
lines.xiang: The team horse losing one horse means cutting off the kind above.

lines.text: He possesses sincerity, which links together. No blame.
lines.xiang: He possesses sincerity, which links together, because the place is correct.

lines.text: A rooster mounts to heaven. Perseverance brings misfortune.
lines.xiang: A rooster mounting to heaven means how can it last long?

lines.text: The bird meets with misfortune.
lines.xiang: The bird meeting with misfortune means there is nothing to be done.

lines.text: Passing by one's grandfather and meeting one's grandmother. Not reaching one's ruler, one meets one's minister. No blame.
lines.xiang: Not reaching one's ruler means the minister cannot pass by.

lines.text: If one does not guard against passing, one will be followed by robbers. How could there be blame? Misfortune.
lines.xiang: Being followed by robbers means the misfortune is great.

lines.text: No blame. He meets him without passing by. Going is dangerous. One must be on guard. Do not act. Be constantly persevering.
lines.xiang: He meets him without passing by means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Dense clouds, no rain from our western territory. The prince shoots and hits him who is in the cave.
lines.xiang: Dense clouds but no rain means it is already above.

lines.text: Not meeting him but passing by. The bird in flight meets with misfortune. This is truly a misfortune.
lines.xiang: Not meeting him but passing by means it is already too high.

lines.text: He drags the wheels back. His tail gets wet. No blame.
lines.xiang: Dragging the wheels back means acting without blame.

lines.text: The woman loses the curtain of her carriage. Do not run after it; on the seventh day you will get it.
lines.xiang: Getting it on the seventh day means following the middle way.

lines.text: The Illustrious Ancestor disciplines the Devil's Country. After three years he conquers it. Inferior people must not be employed.
lines.xiang: After three years he conquers it because he is exhausted.

lines.text: The finest clothes turn to rags. Be careful all day long.
lines.xiang: Being careful all day long means there is doubt.

lines.text: The neighbor in the east who slaughters an ox does not attain as much real happiness as the neighbor in the west with his small offering.
lines.xiang: The neighbor in the east slaughtering an ox does not attain as much as the neighbor in the west because the time is not yet.

lines.text: He gets his tail wet. Just as he is getting his head in the water, misfortune comes.
lines.xiang: Getting the tail wet means the misfortune of getting the head in the water cannot last long.

lines.text: He gets his tail wet. Humiliation.
lines.xiang: Getting the tail wet means not knowing the limit.

lines.text: He drags the wheels back. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.xiang: The good fortune of perseverance of the nine in the second place means acting correctly in the center.

lines.text: Before completion, misfortune. It furthers one to cross the great water.
lines.xiang: Before completion bringing misfortune means the place is not correct.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. He shakes off the Demon's Country. After three years, rewards come to him from the great kingdom.
lines.xiang: Perseverance bringing good fortune and remorse disappearing means the will is carried out.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune. No remorse. The light of the superior person is true. Good fortune.
lines.xiang: The light of the superior person being true brings good fortune because his light shines.

lines.text: He drinks wine in full confidence. There is no blame. But if he gets his head in the water, he loses confidence, and this is a mistake.
lines.xiang: Drinking wine and getting the head in the water means not knowing the limit.
